openQuestions.question: Is any documented or scripted launcher invocation binding a routable address? This scan covered reviewapp/api only; REVIEWAPP_HOST is read at reviewapp/cli.py:116 and defaults to loopback, but deployment scripts, container manifests and provisioning/ were out of scope and would settle the finding's real-world reachability.
pipeline/ (document ingestion) and contracts/ were not scanned — for a system whose input is untrusted documents, the parsing surface is the other high-value target.

surfaces.label: Authentication and authorization (auth.py, route dependencies)
surfaces.notes: JWT-vs-JWKS validation, Entra app-role RBAC with unknown roles dropped at validation so a role rename cannot silently grant access, and a local-principal bypass correctly gated on BOTH a launcher marker and a loopback origin, failing closed on an absent origin. That design is sound. The reported finding is a route that reaches for the same launcher-only concept with only half the test.

surfaces.label: Trustworthiness of request.client.host
surfaces.notes: The loopback test is only as good as client.host. No proxy_headers, forwarded_allow_ips, ProxyHeadersMiddleware or X-Forwarded handling exists anywhere in the repository, so client.host is the real transport peer and cannot be set by a request header.

surfaces.label: SQL construction
surfaces.notes: No f-string, concatenation or .format interpolation reaches an execute/text/raw call in scope. The single f-string hit was a log-prefix builder, not SQL.

surfaces.label: Deserialization of untrusted input
surfaces.notes: No pickle, marshal, yaml.load, eval or exec anywhere in scope.

surfaces.label: Outbound requests from request handlers
surfaces.notes: No requests, httpx, aiohttp or urlopen call in scope; no attacker-influenced destination exists.

surfaces.label: CORS and debug configuration
surfaces.notes: No CORSMiddleware, allow_origins, allow_credentials or debug=True in scope.

surfaces.label: Reflection of caller input in error bodies
surfaces.notes: The corpus 400 deliberately does not echo the supplied path back, and says so in its docstring. Auth failures surface a failure CLASS only, never the token or claims.
